The last edit I made was to sdft/data.py to adjust how the chat template is tokenized. I added a comment explaining the change and switched from tokenize=True to tokenize=False followed by an explicit call to tokenizer(...)[“input_ids”] to get a list of ints. This was necessary because with transformers v5 the return type of apply_chat_template changed, and my earlier code was now returning a BatchEncoding object, causing downstream errors when the code expected a plain list of token IDs.

Now I need to verify that this fix actually resolves the problem. Earlier, when I tried to run a snippet that called expert_target_ids and apply_template to print out token counts and decode the target and teacher prompts, it crashed during the decode step. The traceback suggested an issue with the type of the token IDs being passed to tokenizer.decode. After the edit, the functions should now return proper lists of ints, so decoding should work.

To confirm, I will re‑run a similar diagnostic script: load the tokenizer, read the tools config, read the example JSON lines, and for each example compute the student prompt (via expert_target_ids) and the teacher prompt (via apply_template). I’ll print the lengths of each to see that they are reasonable. Then, for the first example, I’ll decode the target IDs back to text and also decode the tail of the teacher prompt to inspect that the rendering looks correct. This will give me both a sanity check on the tokenization fix and a quick visual verification of the prompts.

I need to execute this in PowerShell because the environment is Windows. I’ll construct a one‑liner Python command using a heredoc (the @' … '@ syntax) to keep the script readable. I’ll also pipe the output through Select-Object -First 70 to avoid flooding the console, but I’ll set a generous timeout (5 minutes) just in case the script takes longer on larger data. The command will change directory to D:\physics\sdft so all relative paths resolve correctly.

Thus, the next step is to run this diagnostic script to ensure the recent edit fixed the tokenization issue. This aligns with the immediate need to validate the changes before proceeding further with any training or data preparation steps. 

Now I’ll issue the PowerShell tool call with the constructed command.

cd D:\physics\sdft; python -c @'
import json
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
from sdft.data import expert_target_ids, make_teacher_context, apply_template

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B")
tools = json.load(open("configs/tools.json", encoding="utf-8"))
lines = open("data/examples_sample.jsonl", encoding="utf-8").readlines()
kw = {"enable_thinking": False}

for n, line in enumerate(lines):
    ex = json.loads(line)
    p, tgt = expert_target_ids(tok, ex["context"], ex["expert"], tools, kw)
    tp = apply_template(tok, make_teacher_context(ex["context"], ex["expert"]), tools, True, kw)
    print(f"example {n}: student_prompt={len(p)} teacher_prompt={len(tp)} target={len(tgt)}")

ex = json.loads(lines[0])
p, tgt = expert_target_ids(tok, ex["context"], ex["expert"], tools, kw)
print("--- target decoded (turn w/ tool call) ---")
print(tok.decode(tgt))
tp = apply_template(tok, make_teacher_context(ex["context"], ex["expert"]), tools, True, kw)
print("--- teacher prompt tail ---")
print(tok.decode(tp[-300:]))
'@ 2>&1 | Select-Object -First 70
